A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RISK framework. All 17 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A.7 report original offline benchmark results, online browser evaluations, and reward analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds optimizer comparisons, component ablations, model-size experiments, and supplementary findings.

M1.justification: The four-component RISK-R1 procedure, DOM-index actions, and staged reward schedule remain intact. However, Equation 1 revises the stated optimization objective's normalization and KL-penalty placement; the PDFs do not establish whether its implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions use RISK-Data, RISK-Bench, OS-Genesis web tasks, and live e-commerce evaluation. The information-search and website-verification tasks remain unchanged; additional model sizes do not expand task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 2 adds explicit GRPO, DAPO, and GSPO comparisons using RISK-Data and the same RISK-SFT-7B starting checkpoint. These substantially strengthen the training-method comparisons; the original offline and online comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds matched-checkpoint optimizer controls, 3B and 32B model configurations, and additional component and difficulty-weight configurations. These extend the experimental design substantially. Existing 7B training budgets, preprocessing, metrics, and inference settings remain unchanged; the metrics move from Appendix A.6 to Section 5.1.

E4.justification: New analyses include the component ablation in Table 4, model scaling in Table 5, and latency/cost and qualitative failure analyses in Appendices I-J. Table 10 expands the difficulty-weight sensitivity study. Existing process-reweighting and reward-schedule analyses are retained, partly relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The five responses used for difficulty grading and eight training rollouts per prompt are unchanged; the new results introduce no uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds optimizer scores, component-ablation results, and scaling results, including RISK single-/multi-step scores of 70.2/62.5 for 3B and 89.4/84.9 for 32B. Additional weight configurations, latency claims, and qualitative failure findings further expand the evidence. The original 7B benchmark scores and 70.5% online success rate remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 1 moves the KL penalty outside the clipped minimum and omits the earlier explicit response-length normalization when expressing the objective as a trajectory sum. These change the mathematics as printed, beyond notation alone. Other reward definitions remain equivalent, and no proofs are added.

C1.justification: The three core contributions and headline performance claims are retained. The abstract and introduction newly claim that RISK-R1 uses only 7.2% of the SOTA baseline's parameters, adding a quantitative parameter-efficiency claim.

C2.justification: Appendices I-J add deployment arguments about latency and cost, and explanations linking failures to instruction following, context limitations, and unseen page states. Section 7 expands the earlier limitations with specific concerns about long-horizon credit assignment, changing environments, and generalization.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link in the abstract and more explicit masking/filtering descriptions in the ethics statement. Hardware, training schedules, image/token limits, and deterministic vLLM inference were already documented in v1 Appendix A.6 and remain in v2 Appendix F.

R1.justification: v2 adds the DAPO and GSPO references and positions RISK-R1 against these policy-optimization alternatives. The existing GUI-agent taxonomy and overall domain-specific positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 reorganizes Appendix A.1-A.7 into Appendices A-J with a contents list, moves limitations into the main text, and relocates process/level-reweight analyses to Appendix G. The abstract, related work, and conclusion are also condensed or rewritten, substantially changing the narrative structure.

P2.justification: The document changes from one-column to two-column layout, extensively resizing and relocating displays. Figure 2 is redrawn with its trajectory-loop illustrations removed; the action-distribution and sensitivity plots move to the appendix. New comparison, ablation, and scaling tables are added, and the action-definition tables are repartitioned.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the controlled optimizer comparisons and component ablations provide stronger evidence for the specific training contribution; scaling results and the code link also help. The net gain is limited by under-specified latency claims, the unexplained 7.2% parameter comparison, and the scaling prose incorrectly describing the 3B model as having the largest multi-step gain despite Table 5.
